question: According to Table 6B-3, what taper lengths are used for shifting, shoulder, and one-lane two-way traffic tapers?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Per Table 6B-3, a shifting taper should be at least 0.5 L, a shoulder taper should be at least 0.33 L, and a one-lane, two-way traffic taper should be 50 feet minimum and 100 feet maximum. The value of L itself is calculated from the formulas in Table 6B-4, and these taper lengths are recommended (Guidance), not mandatory Standards. Guidance (recommended): - "The appropriate taper length (L) should be determined using the criteria shown in Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4." - "A shifting taper should have a length of approximately ½ L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4)." - "If used, shoulder tapers should have a length of approximately ¹⁄3 L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4). If a shoulder is used as a travel lane, either through practice or during a TTC activity, a normal merging or shifting taper should be used." - For the one-lane, two-way traffic taper: "A taper having a minimum length of 50 feet and a maximum length of 100 feet with channelizing devices at approximately 20-foot spacing should be used to guide traffic into the one-lane section, and a downstream taper should be used to guide traffic back into their original lane." Visual evidence: - [Image 3] Table 6B-3 lists taper length criteria: Merging Taper "at least L," Shifting Taper "at least 0.5 L," Shoulder Taper "at least 0.33 L," One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Taper "50 feet minimum, 100 feet maximum," and Downstream Taper "50 feet minimum, 100 feet maximum," with a note to use Table 6B-4 to calculate L. - [Image 1] Figure 6B-2 illustrates the taper types graphically, showing shifting tapers dimensioned as 1/2 L and the shoulder taper dimensioned as 1/3 L. - [Image 2] Figure 6B-3 (referenced as showing an example of a one-lane, two-way traffic taper) supports the 50–100 foot taper application. - [Image 4] Figure 6P-39 (TA-39) shows practical application of shoulder tapers and 1/2 L shifting tapers in a median crossover layout. Citations: - Table 6B-3 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §4 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §8 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §10 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §14 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Support §2 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Support §15 (p.776) - Figure 6B-2 (p.774) - Figure 6B-3 (p.776) - Figure 6P-39 (p.937)
gold_answer: A shifting taper is at least 0.5L, a shoulder taper is at least 0.33L, and a one-lane two-way traffic taper is 50 feet minimum and 100 feet maximum.
